# spread_v1.txt — the D-95 reproducer class: games whose stones sit hex-distance
# 8 apart along one axis, so the candidate count (and with it the cost of a
# full-width iteration) grows as fast as the rules allow per stone. Measured at
# revision 3926110: `go movetime 500` on these positions returned after 644 ms,
# 2334 ms and 14135 ms at 11, 21 and 51 stones (configs/play_v0.toml, release),
# and D-95 records 58.6 s at the 99-stone point.
#
# Stone counts: the WP-1.4 prompt names 10/20/50 stones, but a turn-boundary
# position in this game always holds an odd stone count (turn 1 places one
# stone, every later turn two — rule 3), and a search starts only at a turn
# boundary. 11/21/51 are the smallest turn-boundary counts at or above the named
# sizes; 99 stones (50 turns) is D-95's own worst measured point, added on the
# REVIEW-design finding that the largest measured instance is the one the
# epsilon promise must be measured at.
#
# Every `position` line is a protocol line (docs/decisions.md D-5, D-6). Every
# placement is legal under rule 5: each stone is exactly distance 8 from its
# predecessor. No line of same-colored stones is ever contiguous, so no position
# here is decided. This file is sha-pinned by the test that reads it (D-37).
